title: Kenscoff Gang Releases 13 Hostages — Six Children, Seven Women — After UN Pressure
detail: The gang holding more than 50 hostages seized in the August 23 Kenscoff massacre released 13 captives late on August 29, 2026 — six children (including three under age 2, a 7-year-old, and two teenage girls) and seven women. The United Nations announced the release, which came days after UN Special Representative Carlos Ruiz Massieu briefed the Security Council on the massacre and gang leader Johnson "Izo 2" André's threats to kill hostages if security forces moved against the gang. UNICEF's deputy representative in Haiti called the release "a rare moment of hope amid the violence threatening children in Haiti," while UN officials cautioned the massacre "is not an isolated tragedy" but part of a broader pattern of gang violence. More than 40 hostages, including women and children, remained in gang custody as of the release, and no rescue operation had been reported.

media.caption: Six children and seven women held hostage since the Kenscoff massacre were released on August 29, 2026

title: South Florida Rally Demands Halt to Deportation Flights, Government Action on Gang Violence
detail: Haitian diaspora members rallied on Sixth Avenue in South Florida on August 29, 2026, demanding the Haitian government intensify efforts against gang violence and calling for the release of prisoners held by gangs, while also protesting the Trump administration's deportation flights to Haiti following the termination of Temporary Protected Status for more than 300,000 Haitians. Organizer Alexis Dorman, who had recently visited Port-au-Prince, said "the Haitian government has the capacity to fix this — they have the arms, they have the money." Protester Fabiola Barchelemy said "Haiti is not safe to be sending anyone — it's a death sentence," citing the Kenscoff massacre that killed 47 and left more than 50 kidnapped days earlier as evidence deportees face grave danger.

media.caption: Haitian diaspora rally in South Florida against deportation flights and gang violence
